title: Reduction to a separably closed ground field
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes
of finite type over $K$, and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type
over $K$. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $U_{\Et}$ whose stalks
are torsion of orders invertible in $K$. Form the cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_KX&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\times_KU\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\
X&\xleftarrow{\;j\;}&U
\end{array}
$$

and let

$$
\beta:q^{-1}Rj_*F\longrightarrow Rh_*p^{-1}F
$$

be its exchange morphism, [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. If the
analogous map $\beta_{K^{\mathrm{sep}}}$ in the square obtained by
extension of scalars from $K$ to $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is an
isomorphism, then $\beta$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $L=K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $Z=Y\times_KX$, $V=Y\times_KU$, and write $r_T:T_L\to T$ for scalar extension, for $T=U,X,V,Z$. Write $j_L,h_L,p_L,q_L$ for the maps after scalar extension. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$), so $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $U$ and $X$ are Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], both are quasi-separated. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $j:U\to X$: its source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and its target is quasi-separated, so $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The original square is cartesian, so clause (3) of the same node makes $h$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are precisely the geometric hypotheses needed for the two applications of field-extension base change below.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: check the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses of lem-kun-0f1c; Stacks Tags 01T6 (morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01OY (properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated), 03GI, 01KV, 01K5 and 01KU

proof.text: Regard $F$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero. Inverse image for constant coefficients is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], clause (3), with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, so $p^{-1}F$ is again a sheaf concentrated in degree zero. For a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and the inverse-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] identify $(p^{-1}F)_{\bar v}$ with $F_{p\bar v}$. Hence every element of each such stalk is killed by an integer invertible in $K$, just as for $F$, by the pointwise definition [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Thus $F\in D^+(U_{\Et})$ and $p^{-1}F\in D^+(V_{\Et})$ satisfy the coefficient hypotheses of [lem-kun-0f1c-exchange]; no single integer annihilating the whole sheaf is required.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: verify both coefficient complexes before applying field-extension base change; Stacks Tags 04JC (sites-modules-lemma-flat-pullback-exact) and 0D6D (sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-pullback-composition)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-0f1c-exchange] with $g=j$, $E=F$, and the extension $L/K$, and with $g=h$, $E=p^{-1}F$, and the same extension. It gives canonical exchange isomorphisms
$$
a:r_X^{-1}Rj_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{L,*}r_U^{-1}F,\qquad
b:r_Z^{-1}Rh_*p^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{L,*}r_V^{-1}p^{-1}F.
$$
These are the field-extension comparison maps, rather than arbitrary object isomorphisms. Under inverse-image composition, $r_V^{-1}p^{-1}F\cong p_L^{-1}r_U^{-1}F$ and $r_Z^{-1}q^{-1}\cong q_L^{-1}r_X^{-1}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition].

source.place: Proof, first sentence: the two field-extension comparisons (Stacks Tag 0F1C, etale-cohomology-lemma-base-change-field-extension)

proof.text:
Set $F_L=r_U^{-1}F$ and let $\beta_L:q_L^{-1}Rj_{L,*}F_L\to Rh_{L,*}p_L^{-1}F_L$ be the scalar-extended square's exchange map. All exchange maps here are evaluated at sheaves in $D^+$, so the first clause of [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees], at coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, identifies them with the images of the bounded-below exchange maps under the full inclusions $D^+\hookrightarrow D$. These inclusions reflect isomorphisms: fullness puts an inverse in $D^+$, and faithfulness gives its two inverse identities there. Thus the isomorphism hypothesis and conclusion may be checked in $D^+$. The scalar-extension faces are cartesian by [def-pc-fibre-product], and [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] makes the two outer rectangles cartesian. Apply the horizontal pasting formula, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], in two ways to the same outer rectangle from $U$ to $Z_L$. Factoring the base change as $Z_L\xrightarrow{r_Z}Z\xrightarrow{q}X$ gives $b\circ r_Z^{-1}(\beta)$; factoring it as $Z_L\xrightarrow{q_L}X_L\xrightarrow{r_X}X$ gives $\beta_L\circ q_L^{-1}(a)$. The two composite base maps, and the two composite top maps, agree by the defining equations of the scalar-extension cube. For complete typing, write $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(uv)^{-1}$ for [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] and put
$$
C_X=(c^D_{q,r_Z})^{-1}\circ c^D_{r_X,q_L}:
q_L^{-1}r_X^{-1}Rj_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Z^{-1}q^{-1}Rj_*F,
$$
$$
C_U=(c^D_{r_U,p_L})^{-1}\circ c^D_{p,r_V}:
r_V^{-1}p^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}p_L^{-1}r_U^{-1}F.
$$
Here $qr_Z=r_Xq_L$ and $pr_V=r_Up_L$, so each composite has the displayed type. The two horizontal-pasting formulas therefore give the fully typed equality
$$
Rh_{L,*}(C_U)\circ b\circ r_Z^{-1}(\beta)\circ C_X
=\beta_L\circ q_L^{-1}(a).
$$
This spells out the compatibility needed from the blueprint's phrase 'the pullback of the exchange morphism'.

source.place: Proof, second clause: compatibility of the exchange map; Stacks Tag 0E47, sites-cohomology-remark-compose-base-change-horizontal

proof.text:
By hypothesis $\beta_L$ is an isomorphism. The maps $a$ and $b$ are isomorphisms by Step 3, and the functor $q_L^{-1}$ sends the inverse of $a$ to an inverse of $q_L^{-1}(a)$. The equality in Step 4 consequently writes
$$
r_Z^{-1}(\beta)=b^{-1}\circ Rh_{L,*}(C_U^{-1})\circ\beta_L\circ q_L^{-1}(a)\circ C_X^{-1}
$$
as a composite of isomorphisms; $Rh_{L,*}(C_U^{-1})$ is the inverse of $Rh_{L,*}(C_U)$. Finally apply [lem-kun-sep-closure-conservative] to the $K$-scheme $Z$ and the derived morphism $\beta$: since its pullback along $r_Z:Z_L\to Z$ is an isomorphism, $\beta$ is an isomorphism.
